title: AI Provider Framework
description: Provide a pluggable AI provider framework (Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, future) with a registry, model selection, usage tracking and centralised prompt templates - without coupling to any one vendor.
rationale: A clean provider abstraction future-proofs all AI features. It lets the platform default to free/local inference (Ollama) while supporting commercial providers, keeping downstream AI features simple.
success_criteria: A new provider can be added by implementing the interface + registering it
The same calling code works across all providers
Model selection and usage tracking work for every provider
Prompt templates are centralised and versioned
Local Ollama works with no paid credentials
notes:
## Scope (in)
- AIProvider abstraction with Ollama/OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini implementations
- Provider registry
- Model selection per provider
- Usage tracking
- Prompt templates

## Out of scope
- User-supplied credentials/encryption (EPIC-009)
- Producing model critiques (EPIC-010)
- Allowing AI to influence scoring (forbidden - EPIC-003 stays deterministic)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-001 - providers operate on engine outputs/model data
- EPIC-004 - the unit AI consumes is a saved model

## Assumptions
- All providers expressible via a common request/response contract
- Local Ollama is a first-class, always-available option
- Usage tracking is needed for quotas and cost awareness

## Risks
- Leaky abstraction -> minimal common contract; adapt per provider
- Provider API drift -> version adapters; isolate SDKs behind interface
- Unbounded usage/cost -> usage tracking + quota hooks from day one
- Prompt sprawl -> centralised, versioned prompt templates

## Future extensions
- Streaming responses
- Provider fallback / routing policies
- Caching identical prompts to cut cost
